blocks.text: This chapter records Judah's response to Sennacherib's invasion during the 701 BCE campaign in Judah. The narrative centers on Hezekiah's religious response through prayer and consultation with the prophet Isaiah, who delivers an oracle of divine protection against the Assyrian threat.

sections.title: Assyrian Propaganda and Invocation of Conquered Lands (2 Kings 19:10-12)

blocks.text: Sennacherib dispatches a second message designed to break Judean resistance through psychological pressure. He marshals rhetorical force by invoking Assyrian victories over other lands and their gods: "Behold, thou hast heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all lands, by destroying them utterly." He catalogs Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the children of Eden in Telassar, along with Hamath and Arpad, as proof that no deity could resist Assyrian power. This propaganda strategy reflects the Assyrian imperial system, which combined military conquest with controlled messaging to assert dominance. Sennacherib's annals record his campaigns and claims of submission, though the annals and the biblical narrative present different emphases and sequences, suggesting that each source served its own rhetorical and political purposes.
